payload.title: Wedding RSVP Reminder Wording and When to Send It
payload.excerpt: A wedding RSVP reminder is a short, personal note that brings in the replies you still need before your venue and caterer ask for final numbers. Ready-to-send wording for texts, emails, cards, website banners and calls in three tones, with versions for destination weddings.
key_takeaways: Time every reminder from your own reply date and the date your venue and caterer need final numbers, not from a fixed rule.
Remind one guest or household at a time, and never send a group message that shows everyone's details.
Match the channel to the guest: a text for friends, an email or printed card for a formal suite, a call for older relatives.
Send three reminders at most, and keep one guest list so only the people who have not replied hear from you again.

faq.q: Is it rude to send an RSVP reminder for a wedding?
faq.a: No. A kind, personal reminder helps guests who meant to reply and forgot. It becomes rude only when it is repeated too heavily or sent to a group.

faq.q: How do you politely remind guests to RSVP?
faq.a: Write to each guest or household individually, thank them, give the reply date and repeat the link or reply method. Keep it to a few lines.

faq.q: How frequently should you remind guests to RSVP?
faq.a: Three steps at most: a gentle reminder before your reply date, a personal follow-up after it and a last call if a name is still blank. Contact only guests who have not replied.

faq.q: What do you say when the RSVP deadline has passed?
faq.a: Say that you are confirming final numbers, and ask for an answer by one clear new date. The last call wording above gives formal, warm and light versions.

faq.q: How do I say please RSVP as soon as possible?
faq.a: Give a reason and a date rather than urgency alone: "We are confirming numbers with our venue, so could you let us know by [new date]?"

faq.q: Can family members send RSVP reminders for us?
faq.a: Yes, and it works well. Split the list so each side's parents, a trusted sibling or a family assistant contacts the guests they know, and share only the names and details each helper needs.
